@graph.name: Why does RuF6 fail to oxidise XeF6, at least under these conditions?
@graph.nrr:question: Why does RuF6 fail to oxidise XeF6, at least under these conditions?

nrr:target.label: xenon(VIII) fluoride species: [XeF7]+ salt or XeF8

nrr:effect.note: no redox potentials or Galvanic series exist for anhydrous HF; the authors leave their calculation to others; pure RuF6 decomposes slowly to RuF5 and F2 at room temperature (weeks in nickel); salt formation from RuF6 and XeF6 is essentially instantaneous, so RuF6 decomposition is not thought to be the decisive step; quantum-chemical calculations and considerations of reaction and lattice energies suggest that an ionic solid containing [XeF7]+ cations may be stable; the decomposition of [XeF7]+ cations may be too fast in our case

nrr:evidence.label: Why does RuF6 fail to oxidize XeF6
nrr:evidence.locator: section 'Why does RuF6 fail to oxidize XeF6 (at least not under these conditions)?', final paragraphs
nrr:evidence.quote: So, why does RuF6 fail to oxidize XeF6? Well, it may be that our reaction conditions are not right, yet. ... Under the conditions investigated by us so far, we only observe F2 elimination and no evidence of any Xe(VIII) compound.

@graph.nrr:note: The thermodynamics do not rule the target out; the authors' working hypothesis is kinetic, that [XeF7]+ decomposes too fast.
